gemini-2.5-flash.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a net strengthening of prior year claims provisions by $5.715 million in 2024. This unfavourable movement was primarily driven by deterioration on events such as the Russia-Ukraine war and Italian Storms. However, this was partially offset by favourable non-event experience and changes in actuarial assumptions, which predominantly benefited the Marine, Energy, and Property sectors. Despite these offsets, the overall impact on the syndicate's net claims incurred from prior years was a strengthening.

gpt-5-mini.standardized_narrative: The Syndicate's opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2024 was $1,930.275m. Prior-year development produced an unfavourable (adverse) net movement of $5.715m (included in claims incurred, net of reinsurance), driven largely by experience on prior events such as the Russia-Ukraine war and Italian storms, partially offset by favourable non-event experience and changes in actuarial assumptions (benefiting Marine & Energy and Property). The net prior-year strengthening is small relative to opening reserves (~0.30%). The 2024 underwriting year experienced several significant named losses (Hurricane Helene, Hurricane Milton, Dali Baltimore Bridge collision, Brazil Floods) which impacted the current accident year loss ratio.
